newsitem.title: FRANCE: France offers technical aid to African Congo force.
newsitem.headline: France offers technical aid to African Congo force.

text.p: France would be willing to provide technical support to an inter-African peacekeeping force in Congo, President Jacques Chirac said on Wednesday after talks with the heads of state of Senegal and Ivory Coast.
"France would not join in the force itself but would certainly provide it with support and technical aid," Chirac said.
"We would, in all crisis situations, like an inter-African force under the control of the Organisation of African Unity (OAU) and the affected nations to take the necessary initiatives."
But Chirac did not spell out what he meant by support and technical assistance, which could range from money or logistical support to training, weapons and even aircraft or naval support.

French troops evacuated nearly 6,000 foreign nationals from the Congolese capital Brazzaville following this month's outbreak of fighting between President Pascal Lissouba and a militia under his predecessor Denis Sassou Nguesso.
But Paris rejected a request from Lissouba that its soldiers remain in the capital and position themselves between the warring factions in order to act as a buffer and prevent further fighting.
Senegal President Abdou Diouf, meanwhile, reaffirmed his willingness to provide troops for a Congo mission.
Ivory Coast President Henri Konan Bedie said he was open to eventual participation in an African peacekeeping force but had made no decision.
"An African buffer force is needed, and Senegal is ready to participate," Diouf told reporters.

Eight West African states including Senegal and Ivory Coast pledged at a summit meeting in the Togolese capital Lome on Monday to support an international peacekeeping force for Congo. Togo and Senegal said they would provide troops.
Officials from the eight countries said the force, to act under the authority of the United Nations and OAU, could be put together rapidly.
A similar peacekeeping force is in place in the Central African Republic capital Bangui and has come under fire from mutineers opposed to President Ange-Felix Patasse.
French forces stationed in Bangui have joined the peacekeeping force in firing on mutineers' positions, prompting the mutineers to accuse them both of siding with Patasse in the civil conflict.
But France has insisted its soldiers acted solely in self-defence and had not taken sides.
